web.title: HiPPO Zoo: Explicit Memory Mechanisms for Interpretable State Space Models
web.description:
HiPPO Zoo: Explicit Memory Mechanisms for Interpretable State Space Models
Jack Goffinet 1 Casey Hanks 1 David E. Carlson 1 2
Abstract
Representing the past in a compressed, efficient,
and informative manner is a central problem for
systems trained on sequential data. The HiPPO
framework, originally proposed by Gu & Dao et
al., provides a principled approach to sequential
compression by projecting signals onto orthogo-
nal polynomial (OP) bases via structured linear
ordinary differential equations. Subsequent works
have embedded these dynamics in state space
models (SSMs), where HiPPO structure serves
as an initialization. Nonlinear successors of these
SSM methods such as Mamba are state-of-the-
art for many tasks with long-range dependencies,
but the mechanisms by which they represent and
prioritize history remain largely implicit. In this
work, we revisit the HiPPO framework with the
goal of making these mechanisms explicit. We
show how polynomial representations of history
can be extended to support capabilities of modern
SSMs such as adaptive memory allocation and
associative memory, while retaining direct inter-
pretability in the OP basis. We introduce a uni-
fied framework comprising five such extensions,
which we collectively refer to as a “HiPPO zoo.”
Each extension exposes a specific modeling capa-
bility through an explicit, interpretable modifica-
tion of the HiPPO framework. The resulting mod-
els adapt their memory online and train in stream-
ing settings with efficient updates. We illustrate
the behaviors and modeling advantages of these
extensions through a range of synthetic sequence
modeling tasks, demonstrating that capabilities
typically associated with modern SSMs can be re-
alized through explicit, interpretable polynomial
memory structures.

A key advance toward making memory representations ex-
plicit is the HiPPO (High-Order Polynomial Projection Op-
erators) framework introduced by Gu et al. (2020), building
on the earlier work of Voelker et al. (2019). In HiPPO, the
past of a one-dimensional continuous-time signal is repre-
sented by its projection onto an orthogonal polynomial basis
under a fixed weighting function (or, more generally, a mea-
sure). The resulting coefficient vector, s, provides a direct
and interpretable representation of the signal’s history, and
can be maintained online via a structured linear dynamical
system. In contrast to modern SSMs, where the state vector
is an opaque learned summary of the past, HiPPO exposes
the contents of memory explicitly through its polynomial
structure and associated weighting function.

arXiv:2602.21340v2  [cs.LG]  29 May 2026
HiPPO Zoo
of which contribute to their empirical success on complex
sequence modeling tasks. These capabilities are realized im-
plicitly through learned state dynamics that sacrifice direct
interpretability.
We revisit the HiPPO framework with the goal of extending
it to support these modern capabilities while preserving
its explicit, interpretable structure. We show that many
capabilities introduced in modern SSMs can be realized
within HiPPO as explicit modifications to the underlying
history measure or the dynamics governing the polynomial
coefficients. This perspective yields a unified framework in
which these memory mechanisms are directly represented
in an interpretable orthogonal polynomial basis, rather than
encoded implicitly in learned state transitions. By making
these mechanisms explicit, the models retain the structural
and computational advantages of HiPPO while enabling
principled analysis of how past information is stored and
used.
We introduce a framework comprising five such extensions,
which we collectively refer to as a “HiPPO zoo.” 2 Volterra
HiPPO incorporates nonlinear interactions by embedding
Volterra series directly into the orthogonal polynomial ba-
sis. Salience HiPPO introduces input-dependent warping of
the history measure, allowing the system to allocate mem-
ory preferentially to informative inputs. Associative Mem-
ory HiPPO embeds explicit associative structure into the
polynomial representation, enabling interpretable key–value
memory. Multiscale HiPPO represents memory across mul-
tiple timescales by explicitly embedding a continuum of
HiPPO states. Finally, Forecasting HiPPO makes explicit
how forecasting objectives shape memory, revealing how
different horizons induce different predictive memories and
geometries on the past.

web.description:
HiPPO Zoo: Explicit Memory Mechanisms for Interpretable State Space Models
2602.21340
## Authors
Jack Goffinet,Casey Hanks,David E. Carlson
## Abstract
Representing the past in a compressed, efficient, and informative manner is a central problem for systems trained on sequential data. The HiPPO framework, originally proposed by Gu & Dao et al., provides a principled approach to sequential compression by projecting signals onto orthogonal polynomial (OP) bases via structured linear ordinary differential equations.
Subsequent works have embedded these dynamics in state space models (SSMs), where HiPPO structure serves as an initialization. Nonlinear successors of these SSM methods such as Mamba are state-of-the-art for many tasks with long-range dependencies, but the mechanisms by which they represent and prioritize history remain largely implicit.
In this work, we revisit the HiPPO framework with the goal of making these mechanisms explicit. We show how polynomial representations of history can be extended to support capabilities of modern SSMs such as adaptive allocation of memory and associative memory while retaining direct interpretability in the OP basis.
We introduce a unified framework comprising five such extensions, which we collectively refer to as a "HiPPO zoo." Each extension exposes a specific modeling capability through an explicit, interpretable modification of the HiPPO framework. The resulting models adapt their memory online and train in streaming settings with efficient updates.
We illustrate the behaviors and modeling advantages of these extensions through a range of synthetic sequence modeling tasks, demonstrating that capabilities typically associated with modern SSMs can be realized through explicit, interpretable polynomial memory structures.

web.title: EU ETS carbon price forecasting via VMGE-Net
web.description: # EU ETS carbon price forecasting via VMGE-Net: a variational decomposition and channel-aware GRU framework Scientific Reports. Published: 2026-09-23. 0 citations. ... Daily carbon prices in the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) exhibit non-stationarity, multi-scale fluctuations, and changes in market regimes, which complicate short-horizon forecasting. This study proposes VMGE-Net, a compact forecasting model that combines Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) encoder, and Efficient Channel Attention (ECA). VMD organizes the target-price sequence permitted under the specified evaluation protocol into frequency-specific components, the GRU encoder models temporal dependencies in the fused mode and covariate sequence, and ECA recalibrates the resulting hidden channels without dimensionality reduction. The empirical analysis uses 1994 daily EU ETS observations collected between January 20, 2017 and March 18, 2026, together with 25 market and engineered predictors. Under the diagnostic full-series VMD setting, VMGE-Net obtained an $$R^2$$ of 0.8834, an RMSE of 2.1009 EUR/ton, an MAE of 1.3639 EUR/ton, and a MAPE of 1.92%. Under stricter expanding-window and 252-trading-day rolling-window VMD protocols, the corresponding $$R^2$$ values were 0.8657 and 0.8587, respectively, and both settings remained more accurate than the raw-sequence GRU benchmark. Ablation, repeated-run, sensitivity, direct multi-step, rolling-backtesting, complexity, paired-significance, and block-permutation analyses indicate that the observed improvement is associated primarily with frequency-aware signal organization, with an additional contribution from lightweight hidden-channel recalibration. These findings support VMGE-Net as a computationally compact approach to short-horizon EU ETS carbon-price forecasting, while its generalizability to other markets and temporal resolutions remains to be examined.

web.title: RF-LSTM carbon price prediction based on CEEMDAN decomposition and multiscale entropy reconstruction | Scientific Reports
web.description: In view of the increasing volatility and complexity of carbon trading markets, accurate forecasting models are essential for policy formulation and risk management. This paper proposed an RF-LSTM hybrid prediction model based on CEEMDAN decomposition and multiscale entropy reconstruction. The model incorporates a rolling decomposition–prediction framework to address the nonlinear and non-stationary characteristics of the carbon market. First, the dataset is divided, and the training set is used as the initial rolling window. Within each window, CEEMDAN decomposes the carbon price series into multiple intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). These IMFs are then grouped according to their similarity in multiscale entropy. The grouped high-frequency components are predicted using the RF model, while the remaining components are modeled by LSTM networks. The prediction results are then integrated to forecast the next data point. After each prediction step, the training window moves forward, and the entire process of decomposition, reconstruction, and prediction is repeated until the end of the series. Experiments using Hubei and European Union data demonstrate the superior accuracy and stability of the proposed model. In addition, a composite score metric, combining model error and runtime, is introduced to provide a balanced evaluation of forecasting performance. ... To further enhance forecasting accuracy and reliability, this study introduces a novel Random Forest–Long Short-Term Memory (RF–LSTM) hybrid model. The model is developed based on CEEMDAN decomposition and multiscale entropy–based reconstruction to more effectively extract hidden information from carbon price data. It incorporates a rolling decomposition–prediction framework, which mitigates the issue of information leakage during the forecasting process. In this study, data from the Hubei and European Union carbon markets are used as case studies. The model’s performance is evaluated using four error metrics: Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Additionally, the mean directional accuracy is employed to assess the model’s capability in capturing price movement directions. An extensive ablation study is conducted to verify the necessity and contribution of each model component, while the Diebold–Mariano (DM) test is applied to examine the statistical significance of performance improvements. Accurate carbon price forecasting is crucial for supporting the stability of carbon trading systems and promoting effective low-carbon policy implementation. To address the nonlinear, non-stationary, and multifractal nature of carbon price series, this study develops a hybrid framework (CMRL). The model integrates a rolling decomposition prediction mechanism to adaptively capture the evolving dynamics of carbon markets. Within each rolling window, CEEMDAN decomposes the carbon price data into multiple intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). These IMFs are then reconstructed based on their multiscale entropy similarity to enhance signal interpretability. RF is used to train the highest-frequency part of the reconstructed data, while LSTM is employed to model the remaining part. web.title: Carbon price fluctuation forecasting using an adaptive dual-channel residual attention neural network optimized with white shark optimizer and blockchain-based data provenance | Scientific Reports
web.description: Carbon markets play a critical role in emission reduction and sustainable economic transition; however, carbon price series exhibit high volatility, nonlinear dynamics, and complex cross-feature interactions, making accurate forecasting challenging. Current forecasting models cannot effectively address both time dependence, cross-indicator relationships, and optimization efficiency, as well as data control reliability. To address these shortcomings, this research paper proposes an integrated forecasting approach, named ADRGPNN-WSO. The framework uses Fuzzy K-Top Matching Value (FKMV) to reduce noise, an Adaptive Dual-Channel Residual Group Pulse-Coupled Neural Network (ADRGPNN) to model nonlinear temporal and cross-feature behaviors, and the White Shark Optimizer (WSO) to adaptively optimize weights, a redactable Blockchain with Decentralized Chameleon Hash Functions (RB-DCHF) to provide secure and verifiable data provenance. The experiment with carbon trading data at the Hubei, Shanghai, and Shenzhen exchanges shows that the proposed model has better forecasting performance, with an MSE of 0.0189, MAE of 0.0987, RMSE of 0.1375, MAPE of 5.88, and R 2 of 0.942, compared with the conventional and transformer-based models. Statistical significance tests further demonstrate the strength of the performance improvements. The suggested framework offers a predictive solution based on reliable, governance-conscious forecasting to aid trading companies, risk management, and policy-making in regulated carbon markets. ... The proposed ADRGPNN-WSO framework introduces a novel hybrid deep learning and optimization architecture for carbon price forecasting by tightly integrating an Adaptive Dual-Channel Pulse-Coupled Neural Network (ADPNN) with a Residual Group Attention Network (RGAN), both optimized using the bio-inspired WSO. Adaptive Dual-Channel Residual Group Pulse-Coupled Neural Network (ADRGPNN) optimized with White Shark Optimizer (WSO) is designed to capture both temporal dependencies and inter-feature relationships within volatile carbon trading data while ensuring optimal parameter convergence. This combination, along with blockchain-based secure data provenance and advanced preprocessing using Fuzzy K-top Matching Value (FKMV), makes the system highly adaptive, robust, and accurate for real-world carbon market applications. The contributions of this research are listed below, ... Forecast architecture of ADRGPNN-WSO is initiated with raw carbon trading data, gathered from Hubei, Shanghai, and Shenzhen exchanges, which are initially preprocessed with the FKMV method to deal with noise and uncertainty. The raw data hashes are kept securely in an RB-DCHF for data provenance and controlled mutability. The purified validated data is subsequently input into the Adaptive Dual-Channel Residual Group Pulse-Coupled Neural Network (ADRGPNN), which integrates a dual-channel pulse coupled neural structure for extracting intricate temporal dependencies with a residual group attention mechanism to highlight essential features among technical indicators. The weights of the model are ultimately optimized by WSO which is boosting convergence and forecasting precision by generating accurate carbon price fluctuation predictions for policy decision-making and trading schemes. A block diagram of the proposed approach is displayed in Fig. 1. ... The input data for this study consist of daily trading records obtained from the CSMAR database covering three representative carbon emission exchanges in China i.e. Hubei, Shanghai, and Shenzhen. These exchanges were chosen for their geographic and operational diversity along with establishment periods ranging from 2013 to 2014. The dataset includes nine key technical indicators for each trading day between January 2 2018, and December 30 2022 which includes trading day, opening price, highest price, lowest price, average price, previous closing price, change rate, trading volume, transaction amount, and closing price. These features provide sufficient granularity for capturing short-term volatility and long-term market dynamics. The collected dataset forms the foundation of the ADRGPNN-WSO framework where it undergoes preprocessing, blockchain-based validation, and subsequent forecasting. ... The performance evaluations (Figs. 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11) of the proposed ADRGPNN-WSO model are conducted using historical trading data from the Hubei, Shanghai, and Shenzhen carbon exchanges. The quantitative forecasting metrics are computed strictly on the chronologically held-out 20% test dataset corresponding to the most recent trading period. The model has an MSE = 0.0189, MAE = 0.0987, RMSE = 0.1375, MAPE = 5.88, and an R2 = 0.942, indicating high predictive power, even under unforeseen market conditions. These findings reveal the framework’s ability to model nonlinear time-dependent characteristics and interdependencies across features in volatile carbon-trading markets. ... The proposed ADRGPNN-WSO model achieves an MSE of 0.0189, MAE of 0.0987, RMSE of 0.1375, MAPE of 5.88%, and R2 of 0.942 on the held-out test set. The outcomes validate the ability to generalize to unseen market data from the Hubei, Shanghai, and Shenzhen exchanges. The stable predictive accuracy on the independent test dataset shows that the model’s performance is not limited to model convergence during training but is also robust for out-of-sample prediction. ... , prediction horizon, look-back window size, optimizer parameters (Adam), initial learning rate, and maximum epoch constraints to guarantee consistency across experiments. The proposed ADRGPNN-WSO shows the most favorable results across all evaluation metrics: MSE = 0.0189, MAE = 0.0987, R2 Score = 0.942, MAPE = 5.88, and RMSE = 0.1375. The most successful transformer-based model is TimesNet (MSE 0.0197, R 2 0.940), then Autoformer (MSE 0.0208, R 2 0.936) and Informer (MSE 0.0221, R 2 0.930). This demonstrates that it can capture long-term dependencies. However, it is also surpassed by ADRGPNN-WSO, ... The experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed ADRGPNN-WSO model in forecasting carbon price fluctuations. The proposed model achieved the lowest error metrics i.e. MSE 0.0189, MAE 0.0987, RMSE 0.1375, MAPE 5.88% and the highest R2 Score (0.942) among other compared methods. This shows a strong baselines such as CNN-LSTM (MSE 0.0231, R2 0.926) and TCNN (MSE 0.0215, R2 0.931) by confirming the effectiveness of integrating ADPNN with RGAN for capturing complex temporal and cross-feature dependencies. WSO further enhances training by efficiently exploring the parameter space, which surpass the standard optimizers like Adam. WSR Test shows a significant difference in forecasting accuracy. The ablation study also shows that the deletion of RGAN, ADPNN and WSO results in considerably larger errors and lower scores of R2 that would be indicative of a significant role each of the components would play. ADRGPNN-WSO represents a reliable, well-justified and interpretable forecasting system which contribute in decision-making to market players and policymakers interested in predicting the carbon market price trends, trading risk management, and formulating effective climate strategies. ... This study introduces a novel ADRGPNN-WSO framework for carbon pricing that combined decomposition, attention-based temporal, cross-feature modelling, metaheuristic optimization, and blockchain driven data provenance. The existing methods which focus primarily on predictive accuracy, the proposed model provides additional benefits of robustness, transparency, and secure data management. Experimental results confirm that the proposed framework not only outperforms models in terms of accuracy metrics but also contributes unique features such as FKMV preprocessing for noise handling and RB-DCHF for data provenance that enhance its practical applicability for carbon trading markets and policy design.
